messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing recurring 95p latency spikes from the us-central GPU pool starting ~09:12 UTC. Patterns look like sustained egress bursts on a subset of hosts, queueing up packets and pushing CPU interrupts. Dumped a few traces below.

maya: ```
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 0: root refcnt 2 limit 10240p flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5.0ms interval 100.0ms memory_limit 4Mb
 backlog 0p requeues 0
 tx_packets 123456 tx_bytes 987654321
``` 

maya: I also pulled: dmesg shows repeated net_rx softirq stalls + NIC RSS steering flapping on a couple of hosts.

sam: Do we know if this is tenant-local noisy neighbor (egress-heavy job) or an infra-level multipath issue? Any common tenant ids in the flows?

maya: Early look — same tenants appear, but traffic is spread across multiple NIC lanes due to multipath hashing. When one lane saturates, interrupt consolidation moves work and we get tail latencies elsewhere. So both: tenant bursts + multipath imbalance.

liam: That explains the cross-tenant jitter. Two quick options: 1) throttle per-tenant egress (cheap ops change), 2) pin those tenants to dedicated slices / warm pool (costly). Both have warmup/coldstart impacts.

dana: Can we try soft isolation first? e.g., bias scheduler to prefer warm lanes and enable RSS pinning for the offending flows. If that buys us time we avoid dedicated capacity.

maya: I triggered a temporary egress policer for the top offenders (rule id eg-548). Initial telemetry looks cleaner. Will monitor for 10m.

ops-bot: Alert: egress-policer eg-548 applied to tenant=search-idx-9 on hosts [us-c-34, us-c-37]. Automations: runbook link https://internal.redwood/runbooks/egress-policer

sam: Nice. What's the expected cost delta if we move them to a fractional dedicated slice for steady-state? ballpark?

liam: Ballpark: fractional dedicated (0.2 GPU-slice) adds ~20–30% infra $ for that tenant vs shared with throttles, but reduces tail latency risk by ~3x. Hard to be exact until we profile their token rates & kv-cache warmup time.

dana: Also factor in model warmup: if they go dedicated, we can avoid prefix kv-cache regen which is the real latency killer for short-burst flows.

maya: Agreed. If soft isolation fails in next 30m we should open a quick cost-impact calc and propose ephemeral carveout (2–6h reservation) while tenant negotiates optimize. I'll open ticket.

sam: Please add perf numbers to the ticket (95/99 p99 before/after). Also tag billing so we can show customer tradeoffs.

liam: Can someone add a short note for the SLO board? This could bump us into a mitigation curve for us-central if it reoccurs.

dana: I added a doc stub in the infra-runbook: "multipath-egress-mitigation" with steps to enable RSS pinning, apply egress-policer, and request carveout. Linking here: https://internal.redwood/docs/multipath-egress-mitigation

maya: Update: 5m in with policer = 95p down from 420ms -> 210ms. Improvements, but not fully solved. Continuing monitoring.

sam: Good progress. If it stabilizes, we can keep soft isolation + follow up with tenant on rate shaping and better batching.

ops-bot: Reminder: please paste final postmortem notes in the ticket when closed. :memo:

maya: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
